provenance.measurement: Indicators that measure one concept are combined into a factor by a confirmatory factor model specified in advance: eight political constructs on this panel. Factor scores are best linear unbiased predictions from that model. Sets of categories that sum to a whole enter as log-ratio composites, and all other indicators enter as they are.
provenance.index: The aggregate democracy index is not a node, is not forecast, and is not derived from its components anywhere in this analysis.
provenance.edge_selection: A neural additive vector autoregression (NAVAR) is trained three times. An edge is kept in a fit if removing the source's contribution reliably worsens the target's prediction (false discovery rate 5%) and the loss falls in the group of large effects. Edges kept in at least two fits are shown; those kept in all three form the consensus graph.
provenance.edge_sign: The sign of an edge is the direction in which its contribution moves with the source's most recent value, by majority over the three fits. Edges whose sign strength is below 0.60 are marked weak: their effect rises over part of the source's range and falls over another.
provenance.edge_form: Each edge is classified by the shape of its effect curve. Sign-changing: the effect reverses direction over the source's range. Linear: the effect is about equally steep throughout. Saturating: the effect levels off as the source rises. Threshold: the effect is absent until the source passes some level. Nonlinear: one-directional and curved, but neither saturating nor threshold. The type is the one given by at least two of the three fitted models; where all three differ the edge is marked mixed.
provenance.matrix_order: Variables are ordered so that strongly linked ones sit together. The groupings are an aid to reading and are not statistically distinct clusters: modularity 0.215, against 0.238 in randomly rewired graphs of the same density.
provenance.effect_curves: Effect curves are shown for three groups of country-years: the lower, middle and upper thirds of the clean elections index. The model is additive, so the three curves of an edge have the same shape and differ by a constant: the grouping shows where each group's typical values sit, not different effects in different groups.
provenance.forecasts: Forecasts come from a separate neural forecasting model and are shown in the Forecasts view with their error against actual outcomes.
provenance.dynamics: The earlier dynamics view (impulse responses from a second model built on these scores) is withdrawn. What-if responses from the forecaster replace it.

framing_rules: No result on this portal includes an aggregate democracy index. Every result is for a component of democracy or a related condition. If asked about 'democracy' as a single score, say the index is not modeled and point to its components.
An edge is causal in Granger's sense: the source's recent past improves the prediction of the receiver's next value given everything else. It is not a claim about what an intervention would do.

Edge direction comes from the effect curve, by majority across three fits. Edges whose curve reverses direction across the source's range are sign-changing (form code SC, direction 0): describe them as changing direction, never as positive or negative. Every edge also has a shape code (L linear, ST saturating, T threshold, N nonlinear, SC sign-changing, M mixed); quote the shape with its agreement across the three fits, and never guess a shape for an edge not in the digest.
The matrix ordering is an aid to reading: groups are not statistically distinct clusters. Quote modularity only as the chance_comparison pair (observed vs rewired_mean).

Effect curves are evaluated in terciles of the clean elections index, and because NAVAR is additive the three curves of an edge share one shape and differ by a constant: do not describe them as different effects in different regimes.
Forecasts come from one spatio-temporal graph neural network. Horizons are 1, 3, 5 and 10 years; the ten-year horizon is published without validation and must be labelled so.
The 90% band is nominal: in the evaluation period it held the outcome 80 to 87% of the time at 1, 3 and 5 years. Never call it calibrated.

Accuracy is read beside a no-change forecast. MAE is the headline measure; never lead with MAPE. These variables change slowly, so any forecast scores well; the forecast's margin over no change is small and narrows with horizon, and for some variables the point forecast is behind no change.
Structural (source-only) variables are not forecast and are not moved in the what-if view. Say 'not forecast: structural', never that they were forecast as flat.

A what-if response is the change in next year's predicted value of a target if the source stood 0.5 SD higher or lower, read from the fitted NAVAR contribution behind that edge at the country's own position (direct effect, one year ahead). It exists only where the matrix has an edge and has the edge's direction where the effect runs one way. A null response means the shift would take the source outside its observed range; say 'outside the observed range', not zero. Responses below 0.002 SD are no measurable response.
Per-country forecasts and per-country what-if responses are not in this digest; direct users to the Forecasts and What-if views for any country-specific figure.
Factor numbering is panel-specific. Factors are theoretical constructs; use their display names and, if asked what one measures, its member indicators.

Country ties (borders, trade, learned) tell the forecasting model which other countries to look at; they are not part of the causal structure between variables. The learned ties are a common set of reference countries, not pairwise ties. Why those countries has not been tested: present the closed-autocracy reading as a possibility, not a finding. In tests the ties improved forecasts only slightly.
edges_schema: [source, target, direction(+1 rise / -1 fall / 0 sign-changing), score_median, sign_strength, form_code, form_agreement, retention]; consensus edges only
form_rule: Each edge is classified by the shape of its effect curve. Sign-changing: the effect reverses direction over the source's range. Linear: the effect is about equally steep throughout. Saturating: the effect levels off as the source rises. Threshold: the effect is absent until the source passes some level. Nonlinear: one-directional and curved, but neither saturating nor threshold. The type is the one given by at least two of the three fitted models; where all three differ the edge is marked mixed.

matrix_order.caption: Variables are ordered so that strongly linked ones sit together. The groupings are an aid to reading and are not statistically distinct clusters: modularity 0.215, against 0.238 in randomly rewired graphs of the same density.
matrix_order.meaning: an ordering that places strongly linked nodes next to each other; the groupings are an aid to reading, not statistically distinct clusters

chance_comparison.note: like for like: the best single-run modularity of the real graph against the best single-run modularity of randomly rewired graphs. Quote these two numbers together; do not pair the stabilized modularity with the rewired figure

definitions.fans: row = [origin year, q05, q50, q95] of the level at origin year + h; out-of-sample walk-forward forecasts of the model as fitted
definitions.bands: the 90% band is nominal; see final_table.csv for its realized coverage in the evaluation period
definitions.forecast: production forecast issued from the last observed year
definitions.large_move: probability that the change over h years exceeds 0.5 SD of the node level (fall / rise); large_move_threshold gives that size per node

not_forecast.reason: structural by the ICC partition (S2b, threshold 0.90): the node varies almost only between countries, so it is an input to the forecaster and is not itself forecast

forecasts.band_coverage_note: nominal 90% band; realized coverage 80-87% at 1, 3 and 5 years in the evaluation period

definitions.what: published forecast median against the value observed at origin + h, for forecasts made from the origin year with information available then
definitions.mape: mean of |actual - forecast| / |actual| in the node's own units, percent; defined only for nodes whose values are never zero and never change sign (mape_defined)
definitions.error_pct_of_range: mean of |actual - forecast| as a percentage of the node's observed range; defined for every node
definitions.range_accuracy: 100 - error_pct_of_range; show this where mape is not defined
definitions.persistence: the same measure for a no-change forecast; these variables change slowly, so accuracy is high for both, and the comparison is what shows whether the forecast adds anything
definitions.headline: MAE is the measure of record [V.K. decision, 2026-10-05]: show mae in the node's own units beside mae_persistence, and error_pct_of_range as its percentage form; MAPE is kept in the file for reference only
definitions.mae: mean of |actual - forecast|, in the node's own units
definitions.country_row: [n forecasts, mae, mae_persistence, error_pct_of_range, error_pct_of_range_persistence, mape, mape_persistence]; mape entries are null where not defined
definitions.graph: actual values and the forecasts made are in the country files: observed, fans and fans_full

whatif.definition: What-if responses from the causal structure. For a country and a source variable: the change in next year's predicted value of each variable the source has an edge into, if the source stood 0.5 standard deviations higher ('rise') or lower ('fall') over its last three years. Read from the fitted NAVAR contribution of the source to the target, the same function the effect curve draws, at the country's own position, averaged over three fitted models. One year ahead, direct effects only. A response exists only where the matrix has an edge. A null means the shift would take the source outside the range of values observed for it. Units: standard deviations of the target.
whatif.edge_schema: [source, target, form_code, rise_mean, fall_mean]; all-countries means in SD of the target; consensus edges only; null = outside observed range for every country
whatif.note: Responses are one-year direct effects read from the fitted NAVAR contribution; typically about 0.01 SD; below 0.002 SD treated as no measurable response. Per-country responses are in the What-if view.

definitions.what: The ties along which the forecasting model passes information between countries. They connect countries, not variables, so they are not part of the causal matrix.
definitions.neighbours: Countries whose borders lie within 100 km of this one in 2023. A yes-or-no tie; border length is not used.
definitions.trade: The largest trading partners, with each partner's share of this country's trade. The trade source ends in 2014; later years hold the last shares.
definitions.learned: Beyond borders and trade, the model learned to draw on a small set of reference countries, the same ones for nearly every country. It did not learn ties specific to pairs of countries: every tie on which at least five of the six fitted models agree leads to a reference country.
definitions.hubs: Reference countries: those whose recent history most affects the forecasts of all other countries through the learned ties. Measured by removing each country from that channel and recording how far the other countries' forecasts move. in_top_five_of is the number of countries for which it is among the five most influential; agreed_for is the number for which at least four of the six fitted models agree on that.
definitions.channel_shares: The share of all cross-country influence on the forecasts that runs through borders, trade and the learned ties.
definitions.importance: In tests, the ties improved forecasts by about 1% at three and five years on the century panel, mostly through trade, and by nothing measurable on the modern panel.

ties.note: Per-country neighbours and trading partners are in the Country ties view. The learned ties are a common set of reference countries, not pairwise links; why those countries has not been tested, and in tests the ties improved forecasts only slightly.

not_in_digest: Per-country forecasts, per-country what-if responses, effect-curve values, and majority-only edges are not included; they are in the Forecasts, What-if, Effect curves and Edges views.
